full-house.name: Full House
full-house.explanation: Box 3 has only one empty cell left, so r1c8 must be 1, the missing digit.
full-house.payoff: In column 2, 9 can only go in r1c2, so r1c2 = 9.

hidden-single.name: Hidden Single
hidden-single.explanation: In box 2, 5 can only go in r1c5, so r1c5 = 5.
hidden-single.payoff: In box 2, 8 can only go in r2c5, so r2c5 = 8.

naked-single.name: Naked Single
naked-single.explanation: Every digit except 3 already appears in the row, column or box of r1c8, so r1c8 = 3.
naked-single.payoff: In column 7, 3 can only go in r7c7, so r7c7 = 3.

pointing.name: Pointing Pair/Triple
pointing.explanation: In box 1, 3 can only be in row 3 (r3c1 and r3c2), a pointing pair. So 3 can be removed from the rest of row 3: r3c9.
pointing.payoff: r3c9 has only one candidate left, 9, so r3c9 = 9.

box-line-reduction.name: Box/Line Reduction
box-line-reduction.explanation: In row 3, 3 can only be in box 2 (r3c4 and r3c6). So 3 can be removed from the rest of box 2: r1c4.
box-line-reduction.payoff: r1c4 has only one candidate left, 7, so r1c4 = 7.

naked-pair.name: Naked Pair
naked-pair.explanation: In box 2, r2c4 and r3c5 contain only the candidates {5,7}, a naked pair, so those digits must go in these cells. Remove 7 from r1c5.

hidden-pair.name: Hidden Pair
hidden-pair.explanation: In box 2, the digits 4 and 8 can only go in r2c4 and r3c4, a hidden pair. So these cells cannot hold anything else: remove 7 from r3c4.

naked-triple.name: Naked Triple
naked-triple.explanation: In row 7, r7c1, r7c6 and r7c8 contain only the candidates {4,5,6}, a naked triple, so those digits must go in these cells. Remove 5 from r7c9.

hidden-triple.name: Hidden Triple
hidden-triple.explanation: In box 1, the digits 6, 7 and 8 can only go in r1c1, r3c1 and r3c3, a hidden triple. So these cells cannot hold anything else: remove 9 from r3c3.

x-wing.name: X-Wing
x-wing.explanation: X-Wing on 2: in columns 3 and 6, 2 can only go in rows 3 and 5. One 2 per base line fills each of those rows, so remove 2 from r3c5.

skyscraper.name: Skyscraper
skyscraper.explanation: Skyscraper on 1: row 5 and row 9 each have 1 in only two cells, and r5c4 and r9c4 line up in column 4 (only one of them can be 1), so at least one of r5c1 and r9c3 is 1 (chain 1r5c1 = 1r5c4 – 1r9c4 = 1r9c3). Remove 1 from r6c3, which sees both.
skyscraper.payoff: In column 3, 1 can only go in r9c3, so r9c3 = 1.

two-string-kite.name: Two-String Kite
two-string-kite.explanation: Two-string kite on 4: row 2 and column 3 each have 4 in only two cells, and r2c1 and r1c3 share box 1 (only one of them can be 4), so at least one of r2c5 and r8c3 is 4 (chain 4r2c5 = 4r2c1 – 4r1c3 = 4r8c3). Remove 4 from r8c5, which sees both.
two-string-kite.payoff: r8c5 has only one candidate left, 9, so r8c5 = 9.

xy-wing.name: XY-Wing
xy-wing.explanation: XY-Wing: pivot r7c3 {6,7} sees r7c8 {5,6} and r8c1 {5,7}. Whether the pivot is 6 or 7, one of the pincers must be 5, so remove 5 from r8c8.
xy-wing.payoff: In box 9, 5 can only go in r7c8, so r7c8 = 5.

xyz-wing.name: XYZ-Wing
xyz-wing.explanation: XYZ-Wing: pivot r5c4 {4,7,8} sees r3c4 {7,8} and r6c6 {4,8}. One of these three cells must be 8, so remove 8 from r4c4, which sees all three.
xyz-wing.payoff: In row 4, 8 can only go in r4c7, so r4c7 = 8.

simple-coloring.name: Simple Colouring
simple-coloring.explanation: Simple colouring on 4: colour the chain of conjugate pairs alternately; one colour holds all the 4s. r3c9 sees both a blue and an orange cell, so remove 4 from it.

swordfish.name: Swordfish
swordfish.explanation: Swordfish on 3: in columns 1, 7 and 9, 3 can only go in rows 1, 6 and 9. One 3 per base line fills each of those rows, so remove 3 from r1c2 and r9c8.

naked-quad.name: Naked Quad
naked-quad.explanation: In box 2, r1c5, r1c6, r2c5 and r3c5 contain only the candidates {3,4,6,8}, a naked quad, so those digits must go in these cells. Remove 8 from r2c6.

hidden-quad.name: Hidden Quad
hidden-quad.explanation: In row 6, the digits 2, 5, 6 and 8 can only go in r6c2, r6c7, r6c8 and r6c9, a hidden quad. So these cells cannot hold anything else: remove 1 from r6c9.

turbot-fish.name: Turbot Fish
turbot-fish.explanation: Turbot fish on 3: r7c1 and r7c8 are the only places for 3 in row 7, r1c8 and r3c9 are the only places in box 3, and r7c8 sees r1c8, so at least one of r7c1 and r3c9 is 3 (chain 3r7c1 = 3r7c8 – 3r1c8 = 3r3c9). Remove 3 from r3c1, which sees both.
turbot-fish.payoff: In column 1, 3 can only go in r7c1, so r7c1 = 3.

w-wing.name: W-Wing
w-wing.explanation: W-Wing: r4c4 and r5c2 both hold {2,3}, and 3 in r6c5–r6c2 is a conjugate pair linking them. They cannot both be 3, so one of them is 2: remove 2 from r5c6.
w-wing.payoff: In row 5, 2 can only go in r5c2, so r5c2 = 2.

unique-rectangle-1.name: Unique Rectangle Type 1
unique-rectangle-1.explanation: Unique rectangle: r3c4, r3c6 and r8c6 can only be {3,9}. If r8c4 were also 3 or 9, the four corners could swap 3 and 9 and the puzzle would have two solutions, so remove {3,9} from r8c4.
unique-rectangle-1.payoff: r8c4 has only one candidate left, 2, so r8c4 = 2.

unique-rectangle-2.name: Unique Rectangle Type 2
unique-rectangle-2.explanation: Unique rectangle type 2: r5c5 and r7c5 are exactly {5,6} and r5c6 and r7c6 are {5,6,8}. To avoid two solutions one of r5c6 and r7c6 must be 8, so remove 8 from r4c6, which sees both.
unique-rectangle-2.payoff: r4c6 has only one candidate left, 1, so r4c6 = 1.

unique-rectangle-4.name: Unique Rectangle Type 4
unique-rectangle-4.explanation: Unique rectangle type 4: r6c1 and r6c3 are exactly {4,5}, and in row 7 5 can only go in r7c1 and r7c3. One of them is 5, so neither can be 4 without creating two solutions: remove 4 from r7c1 and r7c3.
unique-rectangle-4.payoff: In row 7, 4 can only go in r7c6, so r7c6 = 4.

bug-plus-one.name: BUG+1
bug-plus-one.explanation: BUG+1: every empty cell has two candidates except r7c1, and 6 appears three times in its row, column and box. Without 6 there, the grid would be a deadly pattern with no unique solution, so r7c1 = 6.
bug-plus-one.payoff: In box 7, 2 can only go in r8c1, so r8c1 = 2.

finned-x-wing.name: Finned X-Wing
finned-x-wing.explanation: Finned X-Wing on 4: in columns 3 and 7, 4 is limited to rows 5 and 7 except for the fin at r9c3 in box 7. Either the fish holds or a fin is 4; both remove 4 from r7c2, which is in a cover row and sees the fin.

jellyfish.name: Jellyfish
jellyfish.explanation: Jellyfish on 3: in rows 1, 2, 5 and 8, 3 can only go in columns 2, 3, 8 and 9. One 3 per base line fills each of those columns, so remove 3 from r4c8, r6c2 and r9c3.

finned-swordfish.name: Finned Swordfish
finned-swordfish.explanation: Sashimi Swordfish on 3: in columns 3, 6 and 8, 3 is limited to rows 2, 5 and 8 except for the fin at r1c8 in box 3. Either the fish holds or a fin is 3; both remove 3 from r2c9, which is in a cover row and sees the fin.
finned-swordfish.payoff: In box 3, 3 can only go in r1c8, so r1c8 = 3.

x-chain.name: X-Chain
x-chain.explanation: X-Chain on 6: 6r1c5 = 6r7c5 – 6r9c6 = 6r9c1 – 6r3c1 = 6r3c7 ("=" means at least one is true, "–" means at most one is true). So r1c5 is 6 or r3c7 is 6; remove 6 from r1c7, since it conflicts with both ends.
x-chain.payoff: r1c7 has only one candidate left, 4, so r1c7 = 4.

xy-chain.name: XY-Chain
xy-chain.explanation: XY-Chain: 8r3c3 = 9r3c3 – 9r5c3 = 4r5c3 – 4r5c9 = 7r5c9 – 7r8c9 = 8r8c9 ("=" means at least one is true, "–" means at most one is true). So r3c3 is 8 or r8c9 is 8; remove 8 from r3c9, since it conflicts with both ends.
xy-chain.payoff: In box 3, 8 can only go in r1c8, so r1c8 = 8.

aic.name: Alternating Inference Chain
aic.explanation: Alternating inference chain: 4r5c6 = 2r5c6 – 2r5c8 = 9r5c8 – 9r5c5 = 9r6c5 ("=" means at least one is true, "–" means at most one is true). So r5c6 is 4 or r6c5 is 9; remove 4 from r6c5, since it conflicts with both ends.
aic.payoff: In row 6, 4 can only go in r6c9, so r6c9 = 4.

als-xz.name: ALS-XZ
als-xz.explanation: ALS-XZ: r7c1 {5,6} in row 7 and r7c8, r7c9 and r8c7 {2,4,5,6} in box 9 are almost locked sets that cannot both contain 5 (every 5 in one sees every 5 in the other), so one of them is locked without 5 and must contain 6. Remove 6 from r7c5, which sees all of those cells.

sue-de-coq.name: Sue de Coq
sue-de-coq.explanation: Sue de Coq: r8c4 and r8c6 (where box 8 meets row 8) hold {1,5,7,8,9}; together with r8c2 {1,9} in the row and r7c5 and r9c4 {5,7,8} in the box, 5 cells hold exactly 5 digits. So {1,9} stay in row 8 and {5,7,8} stay in box 8: remove 5 and 8 from r7c6.

forcing-chain.name: Forcing Chain
forcing-chain.explanation: Forcing chain (contradiction): if r5c9 were 1, singles would follow (r5c9 = 1 → r7c3 = 1), and then 1 would have no place left in box 9. So r5c9 cannot be 1.
forcing-chain.payoff: r5c9 has only one candidate left, 8, so r5c9 = 8.
